newsitem.title: UK: Britain's Lotus to detail new partner on Wednesday.
newsitem.headline: Britain's Lotus to detail new partner on Wednesday.

text.p: Britain's Group Lotus Ltd said on Tuesday it would be giving details of its plans for a new partner and for the future at a news conference on Wednesday.
Lotus's Italian owner Romano Artioli has been seeking a new partner to take up a stake in the automotive engineer and sportscar maker for much of this year.
There have been many rumours of the likely partner's identity, with Asian groups Daewoo of South Korea and Malaysia's Proton having the highest profile.
However, on Tuesday afternoon no one at Lotus was available to provide any more details of who the partner is.
In mid-September Artioli promised his staff he would announce a new partner for Lotus "within days".

By early October, however, Daewoo, the only company to have confirmed that it was actually in talks to buy Lotus, said negotiations had broken down as the two parties had failed to narrow down their differences.
Daewoo appeared to leave the door open, saying it could see talks resuming if a compromise were found.
Then last week another player entered the frame via a report in the Asian Wall Street saying Malaysia's Perusahaan Otomobil Nasional Bhd (Proton) would buy 80 percent of the company.
Neither Proton nor Lotus would comment on the report, which said the stake would cost Proton $84 million in cash and the assumption of about $21 million in debt.
Lotus would say only that Artioli was still looking for a co-investor or a partner, though it stressed it was not looking for an outright purchaser.

Artioli owns the company via the Luxembourg-registered Bugatti International SA group, which in turn is the parent of the Italian car company Bugatti Automobili which went into receivership last year.
